data.title: Do turmeric and curcumin have any actual health benefits?
data.author: hilux
data.article_summary: 姜黄中的姜黄素被宣传为具有抗炎、抗癌等多种健康功效的"超级食物"。但研究显示，姜黄素几乎不溶于水，人体吸收率极低，在血液中的浓度远低于实验室中显示抗癌活性所需的浓度。此外，早期推广姜黄素的关键研究者Bharat Aggarwal的多篇论文因数据造假嫌疑被撤回。姜黄素在严格的临床试验中未能显示出明确疗效，而高浓度姜黄素补充剂还可能导致肝损伤，已成为美国草药相关肝损伤的主要原因。日常饮食中适量食用姜黄是安全的，但补充剂需谨慎。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：姜黄的健康功效是否真实有效

不同观点：
• 怀疑派（thorum）：认为文章缺乏实证，只有轶事证据，无法通过科学研究证实或证伪姜黄的功效。强调补充剂可能有危险性（过量、肝病患者、来源不可靠）

• 个人经验派（collyw）：提供具体案例支持姜黄有效——用姜黄加黑胡椒奶昔一周治愈了网球肘，作为天然抗炎药使用

• 文化逻辑派（anon291）：从逻辑角度质疑——如果姜黄真有显著健康益处，印度应该在相关健康指标上领先世界，但事实并非如此。批评将姜黄当药物看待很荒谬，印度人大量日常食用姜黄却没有特殊健康优势

• 整体健康派（notaharvardmba）：简短提出心身连接的重要性，暗示健康效果可能涉及心理因素

补充讨论：争议焦点在于个人经验与群体数据的矛盾——个体轶事显示可能有效，但缺乏大规模证据支持；同时对将普通食材"医疗化"的商业行为存在批评。

48375079.article_content:
A compound in turmeric called curcumin is sold in supplement form, but what are its benefits?
SOLDATOOFF/Shutterstock
As the temperature drops in Australia, I’ve been seeing recipes on social media for “golden milk”, a mix of turmeric, other spices and honey in warm milk. In addition to being delicious, it is meant to have medicinal qualities, thanks to a compound in turmeric called curcumin, which gives it its distinct yellow colour. Curcumin is said to have anti-inflammatory properties that are protective against cancer, arthritis, hay fever, Alzheimer’s disease, menopause symptoms and many other ailments. But is this based on solid evidence?
Turmeric has been used in South Asian cooking and medicine for thousands of years, but has been exalted as a “superfood” in the West over the past couple of decades. This is largely thanks to the research of
Bharat Aggarwal
, a biochemist formerly at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. Starting in the early 2000s, he published over 100 papers showing that curcumin reduces inflammation and kills “
almost all types
” of tumour cells. This sparked the popularity of the turmeric latte and curcumin supplements, and inspired a bevy of other studies. US health agencies have spent more than
$275 million
on curcumin research since 1990, with a large uptick following Aggarwal’s early work.
Read more
Low on energy? A new understanding of rest could help revitalise you
Advertisement
The idea that a tasty, vibrant-coloured spice rooted in traditional Ayurvedic medicine might be a modern medical panacea has appeal. But a large question mark now hangs over the validity of Aggarwal’s research findings. In 2012, the Office of Research Integrity at the US Department of Health and Human Services notified MD Anderson Cancer Center about allegations by academic whistleblowers of potentially fraudulent results in
at least 65 of Aggarwal’s papers
(although that does not mean that the results are in fact fraudulent). Aggarwal left the cancer centre after an internal investigation and
30 of his papers have now been retracted
from scientific journals based on concerns about the authenticity of the results. Aggarwal’s papers, of which there are several hundred, are still regularly cited.
New Scientist
was unable to reach him for comment.
Personally, I find it surprising that curcumin has managed to attract so much research attention because a quick look at its chemistry tells you it is unlikely to be much good as a drug. Years ago, when I did a PhD in cancer drug development, one of my lab colleagues experimented with curcumin, but found it almost impossible to work with because of its poor solubility and tendency to degrade. A 2017
review
in the
Journal of Medicinal Chemistry
, led by
Kathryn Nelson
at the University of Minnesota, concluded that “curcumin is an unstable, reactive, nonbioavailable compound and, therefore, a highly improbable lead” for therapeutic use.
Because very little curcumin dissolves in water, it isn’t easily absorbed into the blood following ingestion. Instead, most of it stays in the gut and is excreted in faeces. A study published by Dutch researchers last year found that
curcumin was barely detectable in the bloodstreams of men
who took curcumin supplements, even high doses of “enhanced” formulations meant to boost absorption with piperidine from black pepper or nanoparticle delivery systems. The concentrations detected in the volunteers’ blood were more than 100 times lower than those that have shown activity against cancer cells in a dish.
This probably explains why curcumin has failed to show convincing benefits in any rigorous clinical trials of people with
cancer
,
arthritis
or other conditions. According to Nelson and her colleagues, curcumin is “a missile that continually blows up on the launch pad, never reaching the atmosphere or its intended target(s).”
Too much of a good thing
Concerns have also been raised about the safety of turmeric and curcumin supplements. Turmeric is safe to eat in curries and other meals because small amounts are mixed with other ingredients. Moreover, only around 5 per cent of the dry weight of turmeric is curcumin. But supplements containing concentrated curcumin, especially enhanced formulations, are digested differently and can cause liver problems in some individuals. According to the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, “turmeric appears to have become the
most common cause of clinically apparent, herbal-related liver injury
in the United States”, with most cases “attributed to highly bioavailable forms of curcumin” like the enhanced formulations the Dutch researchers studied.
Symptoms of these liver injuries include yellowing of the skin, dark urine and nausea. They usually resolve once a person stops taking the supplement, but a
small number of people have died
of liver failure.

data.title: US banks rely on a 65-year-old programming language
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了一个有趣的技术现象：1959年诞生的COBOL编程语言至今仍支撑着全球金融系统。每天处理约3万亿美元交易，支持大部分ATM和美国银行业务。由于早期程序员退休，而大学已停止教授COBOL，企业面临严重的人才危机。替换这些系统成本高昂、风险巨大，往往需要数年时间和数亿美元投入，因此银行选择继续维护旧系统。这为掌握COBOL的新一代开发者创造了高薪机会，公司正支付高额薪酬招募能维护这些关键系统的技术人员。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于COBOL等老旧编程语言在现代系统中的持续使用问题

不同观点：
• **年龄并非关键问题**：有评论指出COBOL（65年历史）与C语言（54年历史）相比，真正的问题不在于年龄差异，而在于语言本身的特性和生态系统

• **实用主义立场**：认为"能用就行"（If it works it works），批评银行等机构不愿投资培训人员，问题在于组织而非技术

• **持续存在的现实**：通过引用多个历史讨论（包括"消除程序员的永恒承诺"、Anthropic对COBOL的挑战、社保系统重建计划等），暗示COBOL"已死"的说法已经讨论了几十年，但它依然顽强存在

• **替代方案讨论**：有人建议转向PL/I，显示对技术迁移路径的不同看法

Synopsis
A 1959 programming language, COBOL, is powering global finance and government systems. As experienced programmers retire, companies face a talent crisis. This has created a lucrative opportunity for new developers learning this older skill. Banks and agencies are paying top salaries to maintain these vital systems. AI is also being explored to help manage COBOL code.
US banks still depend on a 65-year-old programming language and companies are paying to techies who can maintain this critical technology
While tech companies are offering massive salaries to AI engineers, another group of developers is quietly cashing in on a much older skill. Their expertise isn't in artificial intelligence or cutting-edge software. Instead, they work with a programming language that was created in 1959 and still powers some of the world's most critical financial systems.
That language is
COBOL
.

“I can’t come back at 75”: As Nandan Nilekani turns 71, Infosys faces its biggest leadership question
Despite being more than six decades old, COBOL remains deeply embedded in global banking, government systems, and
financial infrastructure
. As experienced COBOL programmers retire, companies are scrambling to find people who can maintain the software, creating a surprising opportunity for a new generation of developers.
What Is COBOL?
COBOL, short for Common Business-Oriented Language, was introduced in 1959 to help businesses process large amounts of financial and administrative data.
Live Events
ALSO READ:
Watch: Anthropic's free Claude workshop that teaches 40 prompting techniques from the team behind the AI
The language was co-designed by pioneering computer scientist and U.S. Navy Rear Admiral Grace Hopper and emerged during the administration of Dwight D. Eisenhower.
Originally intended as a practical business programming language, COBOL ended up becoming one of the most important technologies in modern commerce. Today, much of the world's banking and payment infrastructure still relies on software written decades ago.
The Hidden Technology Behind Trillions of Dollars
Most people never see COBOL in action, but they interact with systems powered by it almost every day. Industry estimates suggest that COBOL-based systems handle around $3 trillion in commerce daily.
The language is also involved in the vast majority of ATM transactions worldwide and supports a significant portion of banking operations in the United States.
Major government institutions, including the US Treasury, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), the Social Security Administration, and the Department of Veterans Affairs, continue to depend on COBOL-powered systems.
This means that although the language rarely makes headlines, it remains one of the most important pieces of software infrastructure in the world.
Why Banks Haven't Replaced It
At first
glance
, replacing a 65-year-old programming language seems like an obvious move. The reality is far more complicated.
COBOL was designed to process financial transactions with exceptional reliability. Over decades, banks built enormous networks of interconnected applications around it. These systems contain business logic, compliance requirements, and operational rules accumulated over generations.
It often requires rebuilding critical systems from the ground up while ensuring that millions of daily transactions continue without interruption.
Some financial institutions have attempted large-scale migrations away from COBOL, only to discover that the process can take years and cost hundreds of millions of dollars.
For many organizations, maintaining existing systems remains the less risky and less expensive option.
A Growing Talent Crisis
The biggest challenge facing companies today is not the technology itself. It's finding people who know how to work with it.
Many of the programmers who built and maintained COBOL systems are now reaching retirement age. Industry reports suggest that experienced COBOL professionals are leaving the workforce at a steady pace, while universities have largely stopped teaching the language.

RP
Rain Paharia
Engineer
I’m the main author of
iddqd
, a Rust library for maps (named after the
Doom cheat code

Omicron
, our control planeâthe software that
sits
at the heart of every Oxide rack, provisions resources like compute and storage for our customers, and ensures the rack stays up and running over time.
iddqd

disks

• **democratization乐观论**（mohsen1）：通过实际案例（非技术背景的伴侣成功构建销售仪表板）证明工具降低了开发门槛，让更多人能创造有用的产品，但同时表达了对自身技能价值稀释的担忧

• **adoption观察论**（okaythisworks）：将此视为white collar工作领域的重大更新，关注点在于市场接受速度和实际应用进程

CVE AI Agent 🛡️
An autonomous vulnerability intelligence engine. Continuously ingests, enriches, and triages CVE data — then delivers findings to your platform of choice via 3rd party tools like n8n, Jira, Slack, Splunk, and/or local file exports.
🎯 What This Is
The
CVE AI Agent
is an autonomous cybersecurity data pipeline designed for
SOC-grade, auditable vulnerability intelligence
.
It runs continuously in the background, fetching fresh vulnerability data from authoritative sources (NVD, CISA KEV, EPSS), evaluating each CVE against your configured risk thresholds, and dispatching AI-generated threat assessments to your workflow of choice.
⚡ Token-Efficient Architecture
Unlike traditional AI agents that "dump" raw data into LLMs, the CVE AI Agent uses a
Deterministic Minimization Logic
to filter out noise:
1K Token Average
: Prompts are strictly pruned to stay around 1,000 tokens (approx. 4,000 characters).
Resource Savings
: Minimal API usage saves money and compute resources while reducing latency.
Precision Context
: Only sends relevant metadata, references, and CVE-specific context, eliminating "context window noise" that causes hallucinations.
The CVE AI Agent is
LLM agnostic
. Additional LLM providers can be added by extending the provider definitions in
config.json
.
The agent follows a strict
Two-Pass architecture
:
Pass 1 (Deterministic):
All measurable data — CVSS, EPSS, KEV status, CWE, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, CAPEC — is extracted from APIs and curated datasets. No LLM is involved. Product names are derived using hardened regex heuristics.
Pass 2 (LLM Enrichment):
The LLM fills only the explicitly marked qualitative sections (Executive Summary, Impact, Detection, Remediation, Escalation, CWE Analysis) using the deterministic context as grounding. If the LLM is unavailable, the agent generates a high-visibility failure notification and a "pure static" report for audit transparency.

data.title: I made my phone slow on purpose
data.author: gcampos
data.article_summary: 作者购买了新iPhone后故意让它变慢，以对抗刷屏成瘾。他开发了VineWall应用，通过限制特定应用的网速来降低使用体验——就像把触手可及的新鲜曲奇变成难以获取的陈旧曲奇。随着持续滑动，网速逐渐降低，视频变得模糊、图片无法加载，最终只剩转圈等待。这种"人为制造的糟糕体验"让用户开始质疑：我真的需要这个"曲奇"吗？通过降低即时满足感，成功减少了无意识刷屏行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何通过技术手段减少手机成瘾和过度使用

不同观点：

• **软件干预派**：推荐使用"One Sec"等应用通过延迟和确认机制打断习惯性打开，或使用ScreenZen等最小化应用。支持者认为足够的摩擦力能创造mindfulness时刻。

• **物理隔离派**：使用双手机策略，将成瘾应用安装在备用手机上并放置在特定位置，强制物理距离来减少使用（从每天4.5小时降至2小时）。

• **系统级限制派**：主张使用Apple Configurator或MDM方案进行深层控制，直接禁用应用和网站，甚至卸载Safari。认为这比家长控制更强大且难以绕过。

• **极简主义派**：直接切换到翻盖手机运行AOSP系统，通过物理界面（数字键盘、小屏幕）本身的不便来抑制强迫性使用。

• **心理根源派**：认为技术手段治标不治本，刷屏本质是逃避思绪/情绪/处境的成瘾行为。真正的解决需要识别并面对回避的问题，否则只会转移到其他替代品。

• **怀疑派**：基于使用慢速手机的经历，认为刻意放慢手机只会让刷屏变得frustrating和miserable，不会真正减少使用。

补充讨论：多位评论者指出Apple的Screen Time功能容易绕过；有人提出设计哲学的反思，认为行业应从"engagement"转向"presence"设计。

48312443.article_content:
May 28, 2026
I made my phone slow on purpose
I bought a brand new iPhone and immediately made it slow on purpose.
by
Guilherme Campos
·
Founder
Last year I got a brand new iPhone 17 shortly after it came out. It was a bit ironic to spend that much on a phone just to build the thing that would slow it down.
Slowing down your own phone on purpose sounds… unconventional, but I had a good reason for it.
For a long time I struggled with doomscrolling. I tried the usual stuff (cold turkey, app blockers) but they didn’t address the craving, and they were easy enough to bypass on top of that, none of it worked.
A thought experiment about
cookies.
How far would you go for a chocolate cookie?
If you had a little machine in your pocket that baked a fresh
one any time you wanted, you’d eat way more cookies than you
do now, probably one every time you got mildly bored.
But if the closest cookie were a four-hour drive away, you’d
eat almost none, even if you love cookies.
Or if there were a cookie in your kitchen, but it was stale, you’d
mostly leave it alone.
The phone, of course, is the cookie machine in your pocket.
So how do you make the cookies harder to get, or less appetizing?
Slow it down!
Making the phone
slow
There are not many options to make a phone slower, but there is one that also happens to be the Achilles heel of
many apps that cause you to doomscroll: Internet speed.
Showing a new video every time you mildly flick your finger up,
at nearly instant speed, requires a fast and stable internet connection.
Knowing all that,
I decided to build VineWall
, an iOS app that can control the internet speed of some apps, and use this
control to make the “cookie” more stale and harder to get.
What
exactly
does a slow connection do to doomscrolling?
It squeezes the apps, tighter and tighter!
Unlimited speed
Capped speed, mild blocky
Right off the bat the speed is capped at the speed of a spotty cellular connection. It is not enough to stop any app, but enough
for the videos to get “blocky” and not look as crisp as we are used to.
As the scrolling continues, the throttling increases and video image quality decreases. Apps that rely on
text content (such as Reddit, X, Threads), will start to show gray boxes instead of images.
Eventually you will spend more time staring at loading spinners than anything else, and at this point a
question starts to sit in the back of your mind:
Do I really want this cookie?
END

This finding, based on an analysis of data from both the U.S. Geological Survey and the National Cancer Institute, is in line with national figures.
Of the 500 counties nationwide with the highest pesticide and herbicide use per square mile, 60% of those counties also had cancer rates higher than the national average of 460 cases per 100,000 people,
according to a recent Investigate Midwest report
in partnership with the Pulitzer Center’s StoryReach U.S. Fellowship and the Fund for Investigative Journalism.
In Illinois, the counties with the highest cancer rates are most often in the central part of the state, a high crop-growing region where pesticide and herbicide use is highest.
Add us as preferred Google source
There also appears to be a correlation between high pesticide use and higher rates of cancer in many other states, including Missouri, Iowa and North Dakota.
Cancer is a complex disease and linked to multiple factors. But scientific research linking pesticides with certain types of cancers has been growing. A
2024 study
in Frontiers in Cancer Control and Society claimed pesticides rivaled smoking in their potential to cause cancer.
Some Illinois lawmakers have pushed for stronger regulations on agrichemical use, including an unsuccessful push during the 2026 legislative session to require a 72-hour notice to nearby schools and parks before spraying.
“There was pretty stiff opposition from the ag industry,” said Kim Erndt-Pitcher, director of ecological health at the Prairie Rivers Network, referring to
House Bill 1596
. “But we all have a right to clean air and healthy places to live and play and work, and these chemicals are trespassing.”

data.article_summary:
这是一个名为 Hermes 的 AI 助手产品介绍，支持 macOS 12+、Windows 10/11 和 Linux 系统。

**核心功能：**
1. **多平台连接** - 集成 Telegram、Discord、Slack、WhatsApp、Signal、邮件和 CLI 等多个平台
2. **持久化记忆** - 学习项目、自动生成技能、记住解决方案
3. **自动化调度** - 自然语言定时任务（报告、备份、简报）
4. **任务委托** - 独立子代理并行处理，零上下文成本
5. **网络搜索** - 网页搜索、浏览器自动化、视觉、图像生成、语音合成和多模型推理
6. **沙盒隔离** - 支持本地、Docker、SSH、Singularity、Modal 五种后端环境

data.author: cyunker
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：佛罗里达州起诉OpenAI的合理性及其背后动机

不同观点：

• **诉讼缺乏法律依据派**：认为很难证明ChatGPT导致谋杀和自杀，类比枪支制造商不承担责任，聊天机器人厂商也不应担责。这类似90年代指责电子游戏"腐蚀青年"的运动

• **政治作秀派**：认为这是DeSantis为2028年总统竞选造势，是政治姿态而非真正解决问题。佛罗里达作为"红州"正在走民粹反科技路线，与德州吸引科技投资的策略形成对比

• **市场竞争担忧派**：指出州级AI诉讼趋势会增加合规成本，将小公司挤出市场。质疑为何只起诉OpenAI而不起诉Google、Amazon等其他公司，暗示与马斯克和Altman的恩怨有关

• **技术责任派**：认为如果OpenAI明知产品在心理健康领域缺乏防护措施，应承担责任。AI公司应记录减少危害的努力，并像理性人类一样引导用户远离有害思想

补充讨论：有人认为"AI"这个术语误导公众高估了LLM能力；也有人将AI争议与文字发明做类比，认为除非反对文字本身，否则批评AI应聚焦于两者的实质差异而非共同特征。

data.author: shenli3514
data.article_summary: NVIDIA发布了RTX Spark超级芯片，将AI计算和RTX图形处理融合在单一芯片中。该芯片配备最高6,144核Blackwell RTX GPU、20核CPU、1 PetaFLOP AI性能和128GB统一内存。支持原生CUDA，可运行AI代理、创作工具和游戏。具有全天续航能力，机身超薄。适用于内容创作者、AI开发者和游戏玩家，支持超过1,000个加速应用和游戏。将推出RTX Spark笔记本电脑和小型高效台式机。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nvidia推出基于Arm架构的RTX Spark平台，引发关于其市场前景、性能表现和生态兼容性的讨论

不同观点：
• **看好派**：认为Nvidia有足够影响力说服主流软件（Adobe、游戏厂商如Riot）推出原生Arm版本，加上Switch的成功经验，为Windows on Arm生态带来希望；对Intel/AMD形成有益竞争
• **怀疑派**：质疑Windows on Arm长期可行性，认为微软无法像苹果那样强制过渡，将长期依赖模拟器导致体验分裂；担心会重演Snapdragon笔记本的失败
• **性能批评者**：指出内存带宽仅为M5 Max的1/2、M3 Ultra的1/3，认为产品表现平平，不适合LLM推理；存在兼容性、功耗发热等问题
• **实用主义者**：关注Linux支持、驱动长期维护（对比Shield的经验）、价格合理性（期待2-3K美元128GB方案，相比Mac 5K+更具性价比）
• **战略观察者**：认为这是对抗本地Mac Mini运行模型的尝试，体现AI供应链各方竞争格局变化，可能冲击Anthropic/OpenAI的商业模式

补充讨论：部分用户分享了使用旧硬件（R9700）运行本地大模型的成本优势案例；有人担心首批产品软硬件问题会损害品牌形象；游戏x86转Arm性能损耗引发关注
